L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: d2e0c11ab7d13c608b83d0e11338f00f5fd7e99a

What I read at this head: all 20 files (+814/−54), the PR body, the card #34794, claim 6947836360 (corrected 6947879967), the seat amendment 6948353285, dev report 6954122169, and the check-runs on this sha. `check-governed-merges` on the final file list: not governed.

Checklist:
- **Shape:** draft, `Fixes #34794`, Clause-② and Metadata-protocol lines in both the body and the changeset.
- **Scope:** every path is inside the claim plus the amendment (`components/.../data-table.tsx`, `context/gridFieldAuthoring.tsx` and their test). `metadata-admin/previews/external-object.test.tsx` sits outside the literal `studio-design/**` / inspector-tests globs. It only re-points its reads of the moved Remove control, so I count it as a test reader of `ObjectFieldInspector`, not as new surface.
- **Changeset:** patches for app-shell, i18n and components, the three published packages whose src moved.
- **Clause-②:** `yes (widening)` matches the amendment: optional `GridFieldAuthoring.columnMenuLabel` plus lazy `studio` keys. Without the member the header is pinned byte-identical. The components widening owes the seat's L2 at `TIER_DEFAULT`. This L1 does not stand in for it.
- **UI strings:** the five new keys are in `studio/en.ts` and `studio/zh.ts`. Every visible string in the new `FieldMoreMenu`, `AlertDialog` and `DeveloperSection` comes through `tr`/`tFormat` with existing keys (`engine.studio.if.more`, `engine.edit.delete`, `engine.cancel`, `designer.field.remove`). The eager en ceiling was read by the dev: 60.4 / 60.5 KB, new strings only in the lazy chunk.
- **Docs:** none made false. `build-without-code.mdx` speaks of Add field only at the package level. The dev's note on `sortability.mdx` is right: it describes runtime grids, which keep the sort click.
- **Tests:** real commands with exit codes. There are 5 ablations, each red on its own case.
- **Unrelated files:** none.

### Must-fix

None.

### Should-fix

None.

### Notes / nits

- **N1 (nit):** `StudioGridAddFieldButton` falls back to a hard-coded `'Add field'` when `addColumnLabel` is unset. Today it is unreachable, because the pillar always sets the label with `onAddColumn`. A keyed fallback, or no fallback at all, would keep the next host honest.
- **N2 (nit):** the en wording runs "Remove “X”" (menu entry), then "Delete the field “X”?" (dialog title), then "Delete" (button). zh reads 删除 throughout. Aligning the en menu entry to "Delete" would make the chain one verb.
- **Deviation 1, judged acceptable:** the collection-time `import '@objectstack/lint'` / `'@objectstack/formula'` lines in the edited suites. They are test-only and required by `check:test-source-alias` (exit 1 before, 0 after). The PR's Tests section declares them.
- **Deviation 2, judged acceptable:** a create through the toolbar Add field is shown by unit test only. Live, the button was measured on screen with the pane open and its click opens the popover. The create itself runs the pillar's same `addField` as the kept "+" column, and `DataPillar.recordsTab-34794` pins the create from the toolbar entry.
- **Header selection is pointer-only.** The capture-phase click selects a field from its header, while keyboard users reach sort and hide through the caret, which is a real button. Field selection by keyboard still has the pillar's other routes. Not a regression; noted for the epic's a11y read.
- **Carrier owed:** the class-a candidate in the report (deleting a published field that holds rows → draft save 409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`, with only the generic unsaved banner and no way to confirm) predates this PR. It needs a filed carrier from the area, not a change here.
- **Overlap:** #34851 also adds an optional `GridFieldAuthoring` member and edits `data-table.tsx`. The dev's overlap-check says it merges cleanly. Whichever lands second re-runs the data-table pins.

### CI at review time

There are 56 check-runs on this sha: 19 success, 13 skipped, 24 in progress, 0 failed. The in-progress runs are Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI and five Lint lanes. **Landing needs every run on the landing head green.**

### Routing

L1 ACCEPT. Next is the seat's L2 at `TIER_DEFAULT` for the components widening. The area lands it after that, with CI fully green.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8239a213b0cf42c851b71f2c89e48a62fb40214c`
Local-runs: none

What I read: card #34794 (body and all six comments: triage 6947138136, claim 6947836360 and its correction 6947879967, the blocked report 6948315503, the seat amendment 6948353285, the done report 6954122169); PR #34926 (body, 20-file list, the net diff against merge-base `b3c3acd3a4`); the L1-a ACCEPT 6954262589; the check-runs on the previous head `d2e0c11ab7` and on this head. To check the #34851 overlap I ran a read-only `git merge-tree` of current `origin/main` (`189358f212`) against the previous head. That is not a build or a test run.

Head move: `d2e0c11ab7..8239a213b0` is one commit (`test(app-shell): drop two unused test imports flagged by Lint UI`), 2 files, +2/−2. It drops `tFormat` from `ObjectFieldInspector.displayPatchReason-28986.test.tsx:24` and `within` from `external-object.test.tsx:13`. No source changed. That commit is the whole fix for the previous head's M1, the Lint UI red. My review of `d2e0c11ab7` (FAIL on M1 alone) is kept apart at `record-d2e0c11-FAIL.md` in the same folder.

CI when I wrote this: **NOT CONCLUDED.** CI had just started on `8239a213b0`: 3 runs succeeded, 5 were skipped, and 15 were in progress (the Lint and Type Check lanes and Check Changeset). Lint UI, Type Check UI and Test UI 1–16 had not been reported yet. On `d2e0c11ab7`, every run except Lint UI finished green. The Test UI shards there were cancelled by the push, not failed. **This PASS holds only if every check-run on `8239a213b0` concludes green. Any red run turns it into a FAIL. Do not post or adopt it until they have concluded.**

Seat check of the condition above: at 2026-11-17T17:05Z every check-run on `8239a213b0` has concluded, 45 success, 13 skipped and 0 failed, Lint UI included. The PASS holds.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`GridFieldAuthoring.columnMenuLabel?: string` (public surface, `@object-ui/components`): right.** The member is optional and the change only adds to the type. In the whole tree the one `GridFieldAuthoringProvider` is in Studio's `DataPillar` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx`), and `useGridFieldAuthoring` is read only by `data-table.tsx` and the new `StudioGridAddField.tsx`. No existing consumer or object literal has to change.
- **`data-table` header (shared renderer): right.** The caret is drawn only when `fieldAuthoring?.columnMenuLabel` is truthy. It reuses the existing `contextMenu` state shape `{x, y, columnKey}` and the existing menu. That menu offers sort entries only where `isColumnSortable` allows, so a non-sortable column gets only Hide, the same as right-click today. The caret's click calls `e.stopPropagation()`, so it neither sorts the column nor reaches the document listener that closes the menu, which keeps the toggle working. The new test pins the header HTML byte for byte with no provider and with a provider that leaves the member unset. With the member set, it checks that the carets are the only nodes added. `headerClick → sort` is unchanged in the components layer.
- **Header click selects instead of sorting, and it does not leak to runtime grids: right.** The `onClickCapture` handler lives only on Studio's `data-records-body` div and is scoped by `e.currentTarget.contains(header)`. It handles a click only when the column is in the draft's own `readFields(shownDraft.fields)`, and it leaves clicks on controls inside the header alone. Runtime list views have no provider, no `columnMenuLabel` and no capture handler, so they keep the sort click. The dev's live check of `/apps/com.example.crm/crm_account` agrees.
- **`StudioGridAddFieldButton` in `renderStudioGridList`'s `toolbarLeading`: right.** It renders `null` unless the authoring context has `onAddColumn` (set only when `canAddFields` is true) and the Studio-local `StudioGridAddFieldContext` holds a value. `renderStudioGridList` has one call site, so the button is off everywhere outside the pillar.
- **Column order through `leadWithNameField` (ADR-0079 D4): right.** It only reorders column names already in memory, held fields first and then the served-only ones. The memo deps gain `draftNameField` and `draftDisplayNameField`, and they still avoid depending on the whole draft. `leadWithNameField` is on main (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts:417`). This applies only to the Studio grid.
- **`ObjectFieldInspector`: right.** The label comes first. `FieldApiNameInput` moves into `DeveloperSection`, which hides its body with `hidden` and does not unmount it, and the `DisplayPatchLock` and rename checks are unchanged. The footer `InspectorRemoveButton` becomes `FieldMoreMenu`, whose `AlertDialog` runs before `removeField`. The menu is disabled when the inspector is `locked` and absent on an external object, the same conditions as the old footer. The confirmation is new behaviour, ruled in seat amendment 6948353285.
- **Overlap with #34851 (merged `e05445e4f5` at 16:09Z, after this head's 16:01Z merge of main): no textual or semantic clash.** `git merge-tree` of `origin/main` against this head is clean (tree `0ab45b61e0`). In the merged tree the provider value carries both `columnMenuLabel` and `...(agentColumnMarks ? { columnMarks } : {})`. In `data-table`, `columnMarks` draws after the header label and the caret draws after the edit button, two separate nodes. Neither test sets the other PR's member: #34851's `data-table-columnMarks-34725` finds headers by `getByRole('columnheader', { name: /…/ })`, and #34851's `DataPillar.copilotChangesLine-34725` reads neither column order nor the API-name chip. Both PRs' data-table and DataPillar pins must re-run on the landing head. They will, because this head has to be rebased or merged onto main anyway.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/34794-studio-records-tab-authoring.md` is `patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/components`, the three published packages whose `src` moved. Under AGENTS.md §Before-you-finish 3, a non-protocol widening with `Metadata-protocol: none` ships `patch`. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` appears at the start of a line in both the PR body and the changeset body. It names the optional `columnMenuLabel` and the lazy `studio` keys, and it matches the seat amendment. **Right.**
- `Metadata-protocol: none` appears in both and is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: none in the done report. Both questions in the blocked report (the confirmation that did not exist, and the components surface) were answered by seat amendment 6948353285, and the diff follows its route.
- Dev out-of-scope: (a) draft save → 409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` with no way to confirm. This predates the PR and still needs a carrier filed by the area, as L1 said. (b) `sortability.mdx` describes runtime grids, which keep the sort click, so the doc is still correct.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No new id materialisation or in-app join. The only data-shaped change is ordering column names already in memory on the client.

**M1 (must-fix on `d2e0c11ab7`), resolved on this head:** Lint UI failed on two unused test imports (`within` in `external-object.test.tsx:13`, `tFormat` in `ObjectFieldInspector.displayPatchReason-28986.test.tsx:24`). Commit `8239a213b0` removes exactly those two and nothing else. Whether the fix holds is decided by Lint UI's conclusion on this head. The dev report and PR body said all 37 local gate commands exited 0, but CI showed this lint error. The ESLint pass over `@object-ui/app-shell` either was not among those commands or did not run on these files. It should be fixed in the dev's gate run, not in this PR.

Must-fix still open: none.

Should-fix: none.

- **N1 (nit):** Studio's capture-phase `e.stopPropagation()` on a header click also stops the native click before it reaches `data-table`'s document-level close listener. So a caret menu that is open stays open when the author clicks another field's header to select it. This comes from reading the code, not from a run. Closing an open menu in that handler, or not stopping native propagation, would fix it. It is cosmetic.
- **N2 (nit, carried from L1 N1/N2):** the hard-coded `'Add field'` fallback in `StudioGridAddFieldButton`, and the en verb chain Remove → Delete → Delete. Both are still open and both are nits.
- **N3 (nit):** the caret is drawn on every column the right-click menu covers, the actions column included. The PR body says so. Hiding the actions column from the design grid was already possible by right-click.

Merge standard: only the nits N1 to N3 remain open, and nits may stay open at landing. Landing needs every check-run on the landing head green, and on this head they had not concluded when I wrote this (see above).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34794-studio-data-tab`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**
